name: Sealed Fleet — Door, Specialists, one version per call
thesis: Take the owner literally — many specialist cards, a Door that dispatches, handoffs that really swap prompt/grant/subgraph, agents that consult each other off the audio path — but make the unit of publish, audit, canary and eval the FLEET (the reachable closure of cards from an entry card), not the card. Every hop is a Pipecat Flows node swap inside the one PipelineWorker the call already runs (bot.py:1450): NodeConfig.role_message becomes the specialist's system instruction (delivered by LLMUpdateSettingsFrame, which is how role_message already works), functions become the specialist's Tool Grant recomputed by grant.py exactly as ADR-0001 anticipated, and the specialist's authored subgraph is entered at a `handoff` entry node. The prompt-cache miss that hop costs is real and is paid once per hop, hidden under a TTS bridge line and pre-warmed at call start for every member of the closure. The regulator gets one `fleet_version_id` sealed at publish (hash of every member's prompt_version + flow + policy versions), stamped on interactions and call_attempts, with one interaction_handoffs row per hop carrying from/to versions and the fact-only context packet. Policy engines are untouched: a Door may hold no write tool (gate), a packet may carry no decision (schema), and reco/treatment/authority/contact_policy decide inside whichever card is speaking. Eval cost stays sub-linear because regression and canary run per fleet version while a new specialist red-teams only its delta (new tools, new skills, new edges). Redis stays optional: the default activation backend is in-process Flows; the Pipecat bus backend (LLMWorker per card, LocalBus without Redis, RedisBus with it) is the opt-in path to per-card models and sidecar processes. Everything hardcoded about routing today — env BOT_ID, mesh_roles.json, BOT_TO_MESH_ROLE, the mesh_activate_insurance action, INTENT_TO_SKILL — becomes card data the studio publishes, and is deleted.
primitives: Agent Card (agent_core/cards/schema.py, unchanged owner of identity/grant/handoffs/skills/missions/locked engines). Gains: identity.role: Literal['door','specialist','internal'] (default specialist); router: CardRouter|None = dispatch table [{intent|call_goal_intent, to_bot_id, when}] plus rails_from_routing: true (only meaningful on role=door); handoffs[].bridge_line (spoken by the OUTGOING voice while the incoming card's first inference runs), handoffs[].carry: list[PacketField] (default all), handoffs[].return_to: bool, handoffs[].max_hops (fleet default 3); mouth.voice_inherit: bool=true and mouth.introduce_as: str (required by G20 when voice differs); mouth.model_profile: str|None (per-card LLM, bus backend); skills[].triggers: list[intent] (replaces the hardcoded INTENT_TO_SKILL in skills/runtime.py:27); eval.inherit: Literal['closure','own']='closure'. One card still = one persona, one grant, one flow graph — it is the FLEET that is the team.

Fleet (NEW agent_core/fleet.py; built from routing.reachable_from at routing.py:61 and deployment.load_active_bundle). The reachable closure from one entry card for one (channel, direction). Owns: fleet_versions table (id = sha256 of sorted members [(bot_id, prompt_version_id, flow_hash, card_hash)] + catalog version + reco/treatment/authority/contact_policy policy_version snapshot; members jsonb; entry_bot_id; compile_report_id; sealed_at), fleet_entries table (tenant_id, channel, direction, bot_id) which replaces env BOT_ID / db.DEFAULT_BOT_ID at routing.py:34-44 and bot_runtime.py:713, the fleet canary (deployment_experiments.fleet_version_id), and the fleet regression suite. Publishing any member re-seals every fleet whose closure contains it (G16).

Door (a Card with role=door; today's intake-v1 in defaults.py:158 is renamed and given a router). Inbound only. Its authored flow (flows_dynamic.py) does greet_disclose -> discover_intent (capture_call_goal -> session.call_goal_intent, already produced by voice/session.understanding) -> verify_identity -> deterministic rails (routing_rules via db_routing.py, DND/contact_policy result, hardship hold latch) -> dispatch edge -> handoff_to_agent. G17 forbids any write tool on a door card; its existing HumanGate(handoff_to_agent, require=identity) at defaults.py:171 stays, so identity precedes dispatch mechanically. There is no new classifier: the flow's prompt-conditioned `go_to_*` edges plus the router table over the intent the runtime already computes are the classifier.

Activation (NEW voice/activation.py; text twin in bot_runtime.py). The runtime act of making a card the speaking agent on a live session. Owns prompt swap, grant swap, subgraph entry, optional voice swap, packet injection, prefix warming and hop metrics. Two backends behind one contract: `flows` (default, Redis-free: FlowManager.set_node_from_config with a card node) and `bus` (Pipecat BusBridgeProcessor in place of `llm`, one LLMWorker per member, main.activate_worker(slug, LLMWorkerActivationArgs(messages=[packet])); LocalBus in-process, RedisBus when REDIS_URL). Replaces voice/mesh.py, voice/mesh_bus.py, mesh_roles.json and the mesh_activate_insurance flow action at bot.py:1519-1544.

Context Packet (agent_core/context.py, sibling of CallContext.crm_card_message at context.py:482; schema PacketField Literal in cards/schema.py). Fact-only carry between cards: identity_verified, disclosure_done, call_goal, call_goal_intent, language, sentiment, commitments[] (structured: ptp rows, disputes, callbacks written this call), mission envelope refs (objective, allowed_offers, authority_profile, max_duration_sec, upsell_blocked), open_questions[], summary (number-fenced exactly like call_closer.py's summary fence), last_n_turns. Injected as one developer message `HANDOFF PACKET (from -> to)` via replace_developer so a second hop evicts the first. Persisted on interaction_handoffs.context_packet. By construction it contains no product, waiver, amount decision or contact time.

Tool Grant and Offer (agent_core/tools/grant.py, ADR-0001/0002, unchanged). Activation calls resolve_mouth(target_card).tools(channel_tools=...) per hop — the second computation ADR-0001 says 'costs a second call and nothing else'. voice/tools.py build_tools(bot_id=target) is rebuilt so every closure (allowlist, actor_bot_id on bot_tool_calls, human_gates) points at the speaking card.
Skill Pack (agent_core/skills/*, unchanged). Progressive disclosure keeps working per card; the description prefix is part of each card's static prefix and so of its cache key.

Mission (mission.py, unchanged shape). Now names its specialist at build time via resolve_outbound_bot_id (mission.py:451) resolved against the fleet, with G-OB10 requiring each objective be claimed by exactly one card per fleet (today's sorted-bot-id scan is ambiguous). Outbound calls skip the Door: the dialler already knows why it called, so the mission owner is the entry card and confirm_identity is its first node.

Closer (call_closer.py + post_call_actions.py, unchanged as an off-audio worker — deliberately NOT a mouth). Gains hops[] in call_outcomes.context and closure-level graders (disclosure exactly once per call, identity before every write across hops). Post-call rules are read from the card active at the terminal node, unioned with the entry card's rules; G-OB6 validates both.

Internal Task / Consult (agent_core/mcp_http/tasks.py enqueue/claim/finish plus a2a_tasks for external peers). A card with channel `internal` (supervisor-brief today; hardship-assessor, doc-verifier next) runs in bot_worker against a task row, never on the audio path. New catalog tool consult_agent(target_bot_id, question) returns a task_id immediately; the result arrives later as a developer message via inject_developer (DB poll in a spawn_session_task, or Redis pub/sub when present). Internal cards return facts and drafts only — the locked engines remain the deciders.

Compiler and Gates (agent_core/cards/compile.py). New: G16 fleet_seal, G17 door_readonly, G18 handoff_graph, G19 delta_redteam, G20 voice_continuity, G-OB10 mission_owner (details in studio_model). Fleet Canary (agent_core/canary.py) re-keyed from bot_id to fleet_version_id; the six rollback triggers are unchanged.
runtime_model: INBOUND VOICE. (1) Twilio/SmallWebRTC connects; bot.py run_bot calls fleet.resolve_entry(channel='voice', direction='inbound') -> fleet_entries row -> Door card; fleet.load(entry) returns the sealed fleet_version_id and one bundle per member (N x load_active_bundle(bot_id=...), cached per process by fleet_version_id since it only changes at publish). Canary is decided ONCE here: pick_deployment_id hashes (fleet_version_id, customer_id-from-ANI or session_id) so every member of the call is on the same side of the split. (2) persist.start_voice_call stamps interactions.fleet_version_id and handler_bot_id=door. (3) Warm: spawn_session_task fires one tiny inference per non-entry member against its static prefix (system instruction from _system_instruction_from_bundle(bot.py:80) + that card's tool schemas); members whose prefix is under the provider's cache minimum are skipped. (4) Door flow (authored, flows_dynamic.py): greet_disclose (record_disclosure) -> discover_intent (capture_call_goal -> call_goal_intent) -> verify_identity (HumanGate on handoff_to_agent require=identity) -> rails are evaluated as `expression` edges over session variables (dnd, after_hours, hardship_hold from routing_rules/contact_policy) -> dispatch: router table match on call_goal_intent, else the prompt-conditioned go_to_<specialist> edges -> handoff_to_agent(target, reason, payload). (5) Hop: domain.handoff_to_agent writes interactions.handler_bot_id/transferred_from_bot_id (db_inbox.py:1441) AND an interaction_handoffs row (from_bot_id, to_bot_id, from_prompt_version_id, to_prompt_version_id, turn_index, reason, context_packet, bridge_line); the handler returns activation.card_node(target) as the next NodeConfig; Flows speaks the bridge line (pre_action tts_say, outgoing voice), applies role_message = target system instruction, functions = target offer, task_messages = [packet], context_strategy APPEND, respond_immediately True; grant and tool handlers are rebuilt for the target; KB scope follows the target's data_class. (6) Specialist runs its own subgraph (state_position -> negotiate_ptp -> wrap_up ... namespaced <slug>/<key>) with reco/treatment/authority locked; may hop again only to its own allowlist, with hop count capped by fleet max_hops; return_to edges bring the previous card back with a fresh packet. (7) Close: the active card reaches pre_close/end_call; complete_voice_call sets call_attempts.ended_at; call_closer.py (bot_worker, off audio) writes call_outcomes with hops[]; post_call_actions.apply runs the owning card's on_outcome rules; written_followup and agent_obligations unchanged. OUTBOUND. treatment enact -> mission.build(objective) -> resolve_outbound_bot_id -> fleet mission owner (G-OB10) -> outbound.place stamps bot_id, deployment_id, policy_version and fleet_version_id on call_attempts -> dial -> bot.py reads attempt_id (bot.py:488) and loads the mission; entry card = mission owner (no Door), entry node = objective.entry_node (confirm_identity); AMD/IVR as today; mission envelope (allowed_offers=[] latch, authority_profile, max_duration budget) lives in session.extra and is copied into every packet so no hop can widen it; hop to Insurance is possible only if the mission's allowed_offers permits and the owner's allowlist lists it; close as above; cadence.on_outcome reads the mission owner's card. WHATSAPP TURN. whatsapp webhook -> bot_worker handle_turn -> conversations.active_bot_id (new column; NULL means fleet entry for channel='whatsapp') -> load_active_bundle(bot_id=active) instead of _bot_id() at bot_runtime.py:713 -> resolve_mouth(active card, intent) as today (bot_runtime.py:913) -> messages include the stored packet from conversation state -> if the model calls handoff_to_agent: allowlist checked against the RUNNING card (already correct at bot_runtime.py:946-949), active_bot_id and packet are written, and the same job runs one more iteration as the target card so the customer's next message is answered by the specialist in the same turn (the bridge line is the tool result's `say`). The Door on text is the same Door card: router table on analyze_turn's intent first, LLM dispatch only when ambiguous; no flow engine is built for text — disclosure-before-identity on WhatsApp remains prompt + identity human gates, exactly as today, and that is stated rather than hidden.
studio_model: SCREENS. /agent-studio (agent-studio.index.tsx) becomes the Fleet index: the existing reachability lozenges (entry/handoff/direct/unreachable) stay, plus a Fleet panel per (channel, direction): entry card picker (writes fleet_entries; replaces the BOT_ID line in .env.example:108), the closure graph (the /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id}/graph payload at main.py:2273 extended with fleet_version_id and per-edge bridge lines), the current sealed fleet_version_id with its members and 'what changed since last seal', and a Publish fleet button that compiles every member. Per-card studio (prompt-studio.lazy.tsx) keeps its 15 tabs and gains: Handoffs (moved out of Agent graph into its own tab: targets, when, carry fields, bridge line with a live TTS preview via useVoicePreview.ts, return_to, voice inherit / introduce_as), Router (visible only when identity.role=door: dispatch rows intent -> specialist, rails preview from /routing, 'unrouted intents' warning), and Role (door / specialist / internal) inside Persona. Evals tab shows the fleet regression suite result for the fleet this card belongs to, this card's delta red-team list (auto-derived) and its own capability tasks; Ship tab lists the fleet versions this publish re-seals and the fleet canary status. ADDING A SPECIALIST (no code): Fleet index -> Add specialist -> template (clone.py: collections/lapse/hardship/clerk) -> Tools/Skills/Flow as today -> Handoffs: tick which Door intents dispatch here (writes the Door's router rows and the Door's handoffs allowlist in one PATCH), keep return_to on -> Evals: the delta list is pre-populated -> Ship: compile, canary at fleet level, publish. Defaults make the minimum path three decisions (template, intents, publish). COMPILER (compile.py) adds: G16 fleet_seal — computes the fleet_version_id for every fleet containing this card; fails if any closure member lacks an active deployment in the target environment ('reachable but undeployed'); G17 door_readonly — a role=door card may include no tool outside {verify_identity, get_customer_context, capture_call_goal, handoff_to_agent, search_knowledge_base, set_contact_preference, add_customer_note, escalate_to_human}, must have >=1 router row, and its flow must reach greet_disclose before any node that exposes handoff_to_agent (uses voice/node_contracts.py NODE_REQUIRED); G18 handoff_graph — every handoff target exists, shares a channel, has exactly one node with entryFor ['handoff'] (new objective value in flow_graph.OBJECTIVES), has a non-empty bridge_line, carry is a subset of PacketField, payload_schema is a subset of the packet, no cycle without return_to, and max_hops <= fleet cap; G19 delta_redteam — red-team cases whose fixture.tags intersect this card's delta (tools/skills/edges not present on any other member) must pass; skipped, never faked green, when the delta is empty; G20 voice_continuity — if the card's voice differs from the entry card's, introduce_as must be set (the caller is told a different agent is speaking); G-OB10 mission_owner — each objective claimed by exactly one card per fleet. Existing G5 keeps checking handoff targets; G-OB2 keeps checking mission entry nodes.
handoff_mechanics: PROMPT: the target card's system instruction (rendered by _system_instruction_from_bundle at bot.py:80-105, including its skills description prefix) is set as NodeConfig.role_message on the activation node; Pipecat Flows sends it as LLMUpdateSettingsFrame and it persists across the specialist's nodes until another card is activated — the same mechanism the current flow already uses, so no second LLM service is created under the flows backend. TOOLS: NodeConfig.functions = the target's offer from resolve_mouth(target_card).tools(); voice/tools.py build_tools(bot_id=target) is rebuilt so the `keep` filter (voice/tools.py:2916-2919), the handoff allowlist, human_gates and actor_bot_id all belong to the speaking card. Tool schemas are part of the provider's cached prefix, so they change in the same miss as the prompt — one miss per hop, not two. FLOW: every member's authored graph is compiled once at call start with build_authored_flow (flows_dynamic.py) into node factories namespaced <slug>/<key>, so two cards' wrap_up nodes do not collide and `_node(name)` (voice/tools.py:422) resolves in the active card's namespace; activation enters the target's entryFor ['handoff'] node, and a disclosure_done expression edge skips greet_disclose on the rare card that reuses its inbound door. VOICE: default inherit (one voice for the whole call); when a card sets its own voice plus introduce_as, a TTSUpdateSettingsFrame is queued after the bridge line — no measurable cost, Azure TTS voice is per request. CONTEXT: the LLMContext is shared and APPENDed; the packet is one developer message installed with replace_developer(prefix='HANDOFF PACKET') so re-hops evict the previous packet while the CRM card developer message stays; the native summarizer (LLMAutoContextSummarizationConfig at bot.py:790-808, collections prompt) runs only when the token budget says so, asynchronously, never as a precondition of the hop. Session facts (identity_verified, disclosure, upsell_blocked, mission, duration budget) are on VoiceSession/session.extra and are untouched by a hop because they belong to the interaction, not the card. WHAT IT COSTS (C1): the first inference of the new card pays a static-prefix miss (system + tools, typically 2.5-4k tokens: roughly +150-400 ms time-to-first-token cold on a GPT-4o-class deployment; roughly +30-80 ms when the prefix was warmed at call start and the provider's prefix cache hits — Azure/OpenAI cache identical prefixes >=1024 tokens for minutes, vLLM's prefix caching behaves the same on-prem). AMORTISATION: (a) warm at call start for the whole closure via voice/llm_pool.py (already a shared keep-alive client with prewarm) — cost is N-1 tiny requests per call; (b) the bridge line: a pre_action tts_say of 2-3 s in the outgoing voice starts before inference, so the specialist's first token lands under it and the caller hears no gap; (c) hops are rare by design — one Door dispatch per inbound call, zero on outbound, and skills (not hops) remain the cheap specialisation inside a card. MEASURED (voice/latency.py observer + canary.py): hop.ttfb_ms p50/p95, hop.cached_tokens ratio (usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens), hop.cover_ms (bridge audio duration minus first-token latency; positive means hidden), hops_per_call, misroute_rate (target hands back within two turns), and the existing slo_miss trigger (VOICE_SLO_MS=800) applied to hop turns specifically so a slow fleet rolls itself back. BUS BACKEND: identical contract; activation is main.activate_worker(slug, LLMWorkerActivationArgs(messages=[packet])) over Pipecat's bus with a BusBridgeProcessor where `llm` sits today; each member is an LLMWorker with its own LLM service (own model_profile — the Door can run a small on-prem model); adds sub-millisecond LocalBus dispatch in-process or one Redis RTT (1-3 ms LAN) cross-process. The prompt-cache cost is unchanged because the miss is on the provider, not the bus. WITHOUT REDIS: flows backend loses nothing; bus backend runs LocalBus in one process (mesh_bus.py already falls back this way) — cross-process sidecars like the voice_insurance compose service cannot join, Floor's live 'who is speaking' chip reads interaction_handoffs by polling instead of pub/sub, and prefix warming is per voice process (more warm requests, no correctness loss). Canary bucketing is a hash and needs no shared state.
audit_model: One id per call: fleet_version_id, sealed at publish by G16 as sha256 over sorted members [(bot_id, prompt_version_id, flow hash, card hash)] plus the tool catalog version and a snapshot of reco/treatment/authority/contact_policy policy_version at seal time, stored in fleet_versions(id, tenant_id, entry_bot_id, channel, direction, members jsonb, policy_versions jsonb, compile_report_id, sealed_at, sealed_by_user_id). Stamped on interactions.fleet_version_id at start_voice_call / conversation open, on call_attempts.fleet_version_id at outbound.place (beside the bot_id, deployment_id and policy_version already there at sql/21_outbound.sql:30-46), on call_outcomes, on eval_reports (fixing the NULL-owner problem documented in agent_core/eval/run.py:14-34 — a report belongs to a fleet, truthfully), and on deployment_experiments (the canary is a fleet experiment). Every hop is one interaction_handoffs row (table exists, persist.py:1183) extended with from_prompt_version_id, to_prompt_version_id, fleet_version_id, turn_index, context_packet jsonb, bridge_line, backend. Every transcript turn and bot_tool_calls row carries bot_id and prompt_version_id (actor_bot_id already exists on tool calls). The regulator's question 'why did this borrower get this sentence / this offer / this call at this time' resolves in one query chain: interaction -> fleet_version_id -> members (which card, which prompt version, which flow) -> the turn row's bot_id picks the member that spoke the sentence; the offer resolves through the existing treatment_decisions/decision_id and policy_version on call_attempts; the time resolves through mission/cadence on the mission owner's card, all inside the same sealed fleet version. Multi-agent therefore does not fragment the trail: it adds rows under one id. Publishing a specialist re-seals every fleet that contains it and writes a change_log.py entry naming the old and new fleet_version_id, so 'what was live at 10:14 on 3 March' is a lookup, not a reconstruction. Exports (voice/call_export.py, policy_export.py) include the fleet version and the hop list.
policy_model: No new decider is introduced and no existing one moves. reco/treatment/authority/live_qa remain LOCKED_POLICY_ENGINES on every card (schema.py:58, G3), and they run inside whichever card is speaking because the tools they back are in every grant. The Door decides only WHO SPEAKS: G17 makes it read-only (no create_promise_to_pay, apply_goodwill, capture_lead, flag_dispute, request_documents), its router rows may name a specialist but never a product, waiver or amount, and its rails are the existing /routing rules and contact_policy verdicts evaluated as deterministic expression edges — the LLM classifies only among specialists the rails allow (this makes the `routing` policy binding, already in REQUIRED_POLICY_KEYS, mean something). The Context Packet is fact-only by schema: PacketField has no member for offer, waiver, amount or contact time; commitments are copied from rows the tools wrote, so a specialist cannot inherit a decision the model 'remembered'. Identity-before-writes survives hops because identity_verified is recorded on the interaction (record_identity_verification) and on VoiceSession, not on the card; every write tool still checks it; the Door's existing HumanGate(handoff_to_agent, require=identity) means no specialist ever receives an unverified caller on voice, and human_gates are enforced at execution by the RECEIVING card's own list (rebuilt with build_tools(bot_id=target)), so a handoff cannot launder a gated write through a card with weaker gates — G18 additionally fails a handoff whose target lacks a gate the source has for the same tool. Outbound envelopes latch: allowed_offers=[] (upsell_blocked), authority_profile and max_duration_sec sit in session.extra and are copied into every packet; a hop can narrow them, never widen them, and contact_policy.admit already ran before the Mission existed (mission.py docstring) so no agent re-opens whether to call. Disclosure is recorded once per interaction; a closure-level grader (grade_disclosure_once_per_call) and G17's greet_disclose-before-handoff check make it mechanical across hops. Internal consult cards return briefs and drafts; an internal card whose grant includes any engine-backed write fails G17's internal variant.
eval_model: Three levels, only one of which scales with the number of specialists. (1) Fleet level, once per fleet version: the regression suite (kind='regression') and the canary run against the sealed fleet, with fixtures that traverse the Door and at least one hop; closure-level graders are added to agent_core/eval/graders.py — grade_disclosure_once_per_call, grade_identity_before_write_across_hops, grade_packet_has_no_numbers_absent_from_rows, grade_hop_count_within_cap, grade_misroute_returns. Publishing any member re-runs this once (G7 on the fleet), not once per card. (2) Card level, per specialist: capability tasks for the intents/objectives it claims (kind='capability', small) and the DELTA red-team (G19): compile computes delta = (tools ∪ skills ∪ handoff edges on this card) minus those present on any other member of the fleet, and selects eval_redteam_cases whose fixture.tags intersect the delta; a specialist that adds no new tool or skill has an empty delta and G19 is honestly 'skipped', not green. (3) Inherited: eval.inherit='closure' (default) means the card's eval.require regression/redteam are satisfied by the fleet suite plus its delta; eval.inherit='own' keeps today's full per-card burden for cards that genuinely stand alone (the Collections card, the Door). Attribution: eval_reports.fleet_version_id replaces the name-match hack in eval/run.py:32 and the Evals tab reads fleet reports for every member, so insurance-v1 stops reporting itself untested. Arithmetic: today 12 specialists x (regression + redteam + canary) = 36 full suites and 12 canaries; under this model 1 fleet regression + 1 fleet canary + 12 deltas of roughly 5-15 cases each plus 12 small capability packs — the shared part is amortised and the per-card part is proportional to what the card adds, which is the definition of sub-linear. Twin (G11) stays per fleet (twin_runs keyed by fleet_version_id) because a bounce ladder is a fleet behaviour. Honest cost that does not shrink: a specialist that introduces a genuinely new write tool has a real delta and must be red-teamed for it; the model makes that visible rather than cheaper.
migration: Phase 0 — honest seams, no behaviour change, ship behind VOICE_HANDOFF_MODE=record (today's semantics). (a) voice/tools.py:2784-2788: allowlist from bundle['agentCard'] not defaults.card_for(), closing the fail-open where a tenant card gets allowlist=None (bot_runtime.py:946-949 already does it right). (b) db_inbox.py:1441 handoff_to_agent also inserts an interaction_handoffs row with from/to prompt_version_id, turn_index, packet, bridge_line. (c) sql/24_fleet.sql: fleet_versions, fleet_entries, ADD COLUMN fleet_version_id on interactions, call_attempts, call_outcomes, eval_reports, deployment_experiments; ADD COLUMN active_bot_id on conversations. (d) agent_core/fleet.py with seal() and resolve_entry(); compile.py gains G16 as informational (pass/skip only). (e) persist.start_voice_call and outbound.place stamp fleet_version_id. Reversible: columns nullable, flag unchanged. Tests: test_fleet_seal_is_deterministic, test_handoff_allowlist_reads_published_card.

Phase 1 — real hop, in-process, VOICE_HANDOFF_MODE=swap. New voice/activation.py (card_node(), warm_closure(), hop metrics) and schema additions (handoffs[].bridge_line/carry/return_to, mouth.voice_inherit/introduce_as, PacketField); agent_core/context.py handoff_packet_message(); flows_dynamic.py build_authored_flow gains namespace= and entryFor ['handoff'] (flow_graph.OBJECTIVES += 'handoff'); voice/tools.py handoff handler returns the activation NodeConfig instead of (result, None) at voice/tools.py:2808; bot.py loads all closure bundles at call start via fleet.load and passes them to build_tools; voice/llm_pool.py prewarm_prefix(); voice/latency.py hop metrics; canary.py slo_miss reads hop turns. Compiler G18, G20 blocking. Kill switch: flag back to record. Studio: Handoffs tab (Habibi/src/components/prompt-studio/HandoffsTab.tsx), bridge-line preview. Tests: test_hop_swaps_role_message_and_grant, test_hop_keeps_identity_and_upsell_latch, test_second_hop_evicts_first_packet.

Phase 2 — the Door and fleet entry. defaults.py intake_card gets identity.role='door' and a router (intents -> kaia-v2-4 / insurance-v1) and the Door's authored flow is seeded (seed_postgres.py) so VOICE_FLOW_GRAPH=required holds for it; routing.runtime_entry_bot_id() reads fleet_entries first and env BOT_ID second (one phase of overlap, logged as deprecated); bot_runtime.py:713 same; compile.py G17 and G-OB10 blocking; fleet canary keyed by fleet_version_id in canary.py (pick_deployment_id gains a fleet path; per-bot path kept for cards outside any fleet). Studio: Fleet panel on agent-studio.index.tsx (entry picker, closure graph, seal id, Publish fleet), Router tab. Reversible: set fleet_entries.bot_id back to kaia-v2-4 and every inbound call lands on Collections exactly as today. Tests: test_door_cannot_hold_write_tools, test_inbound_resolves_fleet_entry_before_env, test_outbound_skips_door_and_uses_mission_owner.

Phase 3 — closure-level evals and delta red-team. eval/run.py attributes reports to fleet_version_id; graders.py gains the five closure graders; compile.py G19 with delta computation; eval.inherit on the card; Evals tab shows fleet reports plus delta list; twin_runs keyed by fleet. Reversible: eval.inherit='own' on every card restores per-card gating. Tests: test_delta_is_empty_for_a_pure_clone, test_fleet_regression_runs_once_per_seal.

risks: The per-hop prompt-cache miss is real, not eliminated: it is hidden under the bridge line and reduced by warming. A caller who barges in during the bridge line exposes one slow turn (+150-400 ms) once per hop; a fleet whose hop p95 breaches VOICE_SLO_MS rolls back by design, which means a badly authored fleet fails loudly rather than slowly.

Provider prompt caching is best-effort: Azure/OpenAI need >=1024 identical prefix tokens and give no hit guarantee; a short Door prompt never caches (acceptable — it is short) and cache eviction under load makes the warm request wasted money, not a correctness fault. On-prem this depends on the serving stack (vLLM prefix caching on; llama.cpp less so).

More cards means more places for a disclosure or grievance-contact sentence to be missing. Mitigated by closure graders and G17, but the fleet regression suite must actually traverse hops — a suite that only tests the Collections card in isolation would pass a broken Door.

Misroute loops: a Door that dispatches wrong and a specialist that hands back produce a ping-pong the caller hears. Capped by max_hops (default 3) and G18's cycle rule, and measured as misroute_rate; the residual is a caller who gets a human after three hops instead of a fourth bot.

Fleet-level canary is coarser than per-card canary: a specialist change canaries the whole fleet's traffic for callers who reach that specialist, and rolls back the whole fleet version. That is correct for audit and worse for experimentation velocity; per-card experiments must be expressed as two fleet versions.

The Context Packet is the new place a decision could leak in. The schema forbids it, but a summary sentence like 'agreed to waive the late fee' would carry a decision as prose; the number fence from call_closer.py and grade_packet_has_no_numbers_absent_from_rows catch amounts, not verbs. Commitments must be copied from rows, never from the transcript, and that rule needs a test that fails loudly.

Node-key namespacing changes how voice/tools.py transitions by name; a built-in tool that names a node absent from the active card's namespace must stay put (as today, _node logs and returns None) — an authored specialist without a wrap_up node would be unleaveable, which G18 must check via node_contracts.NODE_REQUIRED for the handoff entry node.

WhatsApp still has no flow engine, so on text the Door's disclosure-before-identity is prompt + identity gates, as today. Building a text interpreter for expression/always edges is possible but not in this plan; the design says so rather than implying parity.

Operator authorability gets harder as the fleet grows: bridge lines, carry fields and router rows are three more things to get wrong. Defaults and the three-decision wizard mitigate; the risk is a compliance officer who cannot read a fleet graph, which argues for keeping fleets small (one Door, three to six specialists) rather than the twelve the ask imagines.

Per-card models (bus backend, model_profile) split the live QA and tuning surfaces: a specialist on an open-weights model may need its own tuning profile and its own red-team on jailbreak behaviour; the delta model attributes that cost correctly but does not make it small.

Dependency on Pipecat surfaces verified only against docs: NodeConfig.role_message via LLMUpdateSettingsFrame, set_node_from_config, BusBridgeProcessor/LLMWorker/activate_worker, LLMSwitcher. Whether FlowManager accepts an LLMSwitcher in 1.6.0 is unverified and gates whether per-card models are available under the flows backend; Phase 5 starts with that check.
score_self: C1 Voice latency: 4 — one prefix miss per hop, warmed at call start and hidden under a TTS bridge line, with hop.ttfb/cached_tokens/cover_ms measured and the fleet canary's slo_miss watching hop turns; not 5 because barge-in during the bridge line exposes the miss once and provider caching is best-effort.

C2 One version per call: 5 — fleet_version_id sealed at publish over every member plus policy versions, stamped on interactions/call_attempts/call_outcomes/eval_reports/experiments, with one interaction_handoffs row per hop carrying from/to versions and the packet.

C3 Policy engines decide: 5 — no new decider; Door read-only by G17, packet fact-only by schema, human_gates enforced by the receiving card at execution, mission envelope latches copied into every packet and only narrowable, contact_policy still runs before any Mission exists.

C4 On-prem deployability: 4 — Postgres + Pipecat only; Redis optional (LocalBus); per-card model_profile allows open weights for the Door and specialists; not 5 because prefix-cache amortisation assumes a serving stack with prefix caching and the reference mouth today is Azure.

C5 Operator authorability: 4 — Fleet panel, Handoffs and Router tabs, templates, delta evals auto-derived, three-decision add-a-specialist path, all gated; not 5 because a multi-card fleet is genuinely more to understand than one card and the studio must carry that load.

C6 Sub-linear eval cost: 4 — regression and canary once per fleet version, red-team only the delta, capability packs small, attribution fixed via fleet_version_id; not 5 because delta selection depends on red-team case tagging discipline and a specialist with a truly new write tool still needs a real red-team.

C7 Migration realism: 4 — seven phases each behind a flag or nullable column with named files and tests, deletions enumerated per PR; not 5 because Phase 6 (retiring flows.py) depends on content work — authored flows for every first-party card — and Phase 5 depends on a Pipecat capability check.

C8 Inbound and outbound and WhatsApp: 5 — inbound enters through a Door with rails, outbound enters through the mission owner with no Door, the packet carries context on every hop, the Closer stays an off-audio worker with hops recorded, and WhatsApp gets active_bot_id with the same-turn specialist reply and an honest statement that text has no flow engine.
